questions.text: In an Excel sheet, column B holds departments and column C holds salaries for rows 2 to 101. Which formula counts employees in the 'Sales' department earning more than 40000?
questions.explanation: COUNTIFS applies several range-criteria pairs and counts rows meeting all of them.
steps: Spot what the question tests: COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS vs SUMIFS.
Option A (=COUNTIF(B2:C101,"Sales",">40000")) is out: COUNTIF accepts only one range and one criterion.
Option B (=SUMIFS(C2:C101,B2:B101,"Sales")) is out: It adds salaries; it does not count employees above a limit.
Option D (=COUNT(B2:B101,"Sales",C2:C101,">40000")) is out: COUNT counts numbers and does not apply criteria.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing COUNTIF with two criteria.
So the answer is option C: =COUNTIFS(B2:B101,"Sales",C2:C101,">40000").
wrongReasons: COUNTIF accepts only one range and one criterion
It adds salaries; it does not count employees above a limit
COUNT counts numbers and does not apply criteria

questions.text: Which combination of functions can look up a value in a column to the left of the lookup column, which VLOOKUP cannot do?
questions.explanation: MATCH finds the row position and INDEX returns the value from any column.
steps: Spot what the question tests: INDEX-MATCH.
Option A (SUM with IF) is out: Does not perform lookups.
Option B (LEFT with LEN) is out: Text functions only.
Option C (CHOOSE with ROW) is out: Does not search by value.
Common slip to avoid: Assuming VLOOKUP can search leftwards.
So the answer is option D: INDEX with MATCH.

questions.text: Which Excel feature automatically colours cells that satisfy a rule, such as values above the average?
questions.explanation: Conditional Formatting changes cell appearance based on rules.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Conditional Formatting.
Option A (Data Validation) is out: It restricts entries.
Option C (Flash Fill) is out: It fills data from a pattern.
Option D (Text to Columns) is out: It splits cell contents.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Data Validation.
So the answer is option B: Conditional Formatting.
wrongReasons: It fills data from a pattern

questions.text: A long Word document has chapter titles formatted with Heading 1. Which step creates an automatically updating table of contents?
questions.explanation: The table of contents is built from heading styles and can be refreshed.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Heading styles and TOC.
Option A (Insert > Page Number) is out: Adds page numbers only.
Option B (Review > Track Changes) is out: Records edits.
Option C (Layout > Columns) is out: Changes the text layout.
Common slip to avoid: Typing the table by hand.
So the answer is option D: References > Table of Contents.

questions.text: In MS PowerPoint, which feature applies a consistent set of fonts, colours and effects to the whole presentation in one step?
questions.explanation: A theme on the Design tab applies matching fonts, colours and effects to every slide.
steps: Open the Design tab
Choose a theme
It is applied to all slides
wrongReasons: Records the time spent on each slide
Links text or objects to a target

questions.text: In a group of 20 users, every pair needs a separate secret key for symmetric encryption. How many keys are needed in total?
questions.explanation: Number of keys = n(n − 1)/2 = 20 × 19/2 = 190.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Key counts: symmetric vs asymmetric.
Option A (20) is out: One per user.
Option B (40) is out: Two per user.
Option D (380) is out: Counted each pair twice.
Common slip to avoid: Counting each pair twice.
So the answer is option C: 190.

questions.text: An attacker secretly relays and may alter messages between two parties who believe they are communicating directly. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: The attacker sits between the two parties.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of attacks.
Option B (Denial of service attack) is out: It floods a service to make it unavailable.
Option C (Brute-force attack) is out: It tries many passwords.
Option D (Replay attack) is out: It resends a captured message without altering it.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing replay because it also uses captured messages.
So the answer is option A: Man-in-the-middle attack.
questions.trap: Choosing replay because it also uses captured messages.
wrongReasons: It floods a service to make it unavailable
It resends a captured message without altering it

questions.text: An attacker enters a crafted string in a login form so that the database runs an unintended command. This attack is called:
questions.explanation: SQL injection exploits unfiltered input to alter database queries.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Web attacks.
Option A (Cross-site scripting) is out: It injects scripts into web pages.
Option B (Phishing) is out: It deceives users by messages.
Option D (Spoofing) is out: It disguises an identity.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing cross-site scripting.
So the answer is option C: SQL injection.
wrongReasons: It injects scripts into web pages

questions.text: What is the main advantage of instruction pipelining in a processor?
options: Each instruction finishes in fewer clock cycles
Several instructions are in different stages of execution at the same time
It removes the need for a clock
It increases the size of main memory
questions.explanation: Pipelining overlaps the stages of consecutive instructions, improving throughput.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Pipelining: throughput vs latency.
Option A (Each instruction finishes in fewer clock cycles) is out: Latency of a single instruction is not reduced.
Option C (It removes the need for a clock) is out: The clock is still required.
Option D (It increases the size of main memory) is out: It has no effect on memory capacity.
Common slip to avoid: Believing each instruction becomes faster.
So the answer is option B: Several instructions are in different stages of execution at the same….
wrongReasons: Latency of a single instruction is not reduced
It has no effect on memory capacity

questions.text: In a system using virtual memory, what is a page fault?
options: A hardware failure of the RAM
An attempt to write to read-only memory
An access to a page that is not currently in main memory
questions.explanation: A page fault causes the operating system to load the required page from disk.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Paging and page faults.
Option A (A hardware failure of the RAM) is out: It is not a hardware fault.
Option B (An attempt to write to read-only memory) is out: This is a protection fault.
Option C (A shortage of disk space) is out: It concerns residency of a page.
Common slip to avoid: Treating a page fault as an error.
So the answer is option D: An access to a page that is not currently in main memory.
questions.trap: Treating a page fault as an error.
wrongReasons: It is not a hardware fault
It concerns residency of a page

questions.text: Which RAID level uses disk mirroring and so keeps an exact copy of the data on a second disk?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 duplicates data on two disks.
steps: Spot what the question tests: RAID levels.
Option A (RAID 0) is out: Striping without redundancy.
Option C (RAID 5) is out: Striping with distributed parity.
Option D (RAID 6) is out: Striping with double parity.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing RAID 5 because it is 'redundant'.
So the answer is option B: RAID 1.

questions.text: A network uses the subnet mask 255.255.255.192. How many usable host addresses does each subnet have?
questions.explanation: The mask has 26 network bits, leaving 6 host bits: 2⁶ − 2 = 62 usable hosts.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Subnetting.
Option A (64) is out: Counts the network and broadcast addresses too.
Option B (126) is out: Corresponds to /25.
Option C (30) is out: Corresponds to /27.
Common slip to avoid: Forgetting to subtract two addresses.
So the answer is option D: 62.
wrongReasons: Counts the network and broadcast addresses too

questions.text: Which protocol maps an IP address to a physical (MAC) address on a local network?
questions.explanation: Address Resolution Protocol finds the MAC address for a known IP address.
steps: Spot what the question tests: ARP, DNS, DHCP.
Option B (DNS) is out: Maps domain names to IP addresses.
Option C (DHCP) is out: Assigns IP addresses automatically.
Option D (ICMP) is out: Reports errors and tests connectivity.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing DNS.
So the answer is option A: ARP.
wrongReasons: Maps domain names to IP addresses

questions.text: Which device forwards a frame only to the port of the destination MAC address, reducing unnecessary traffic?
questions.explanation: A switch learns MAC addresses and forwards frames selectively.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Hub vs switch.
Option A (Hub) is out: It sends data to all ports.
Option B (Repeater) is out: It only regenerates signals.
Option D (Modem) is out: It converts signals.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing hub.
So the answer is option C: Switch.
wrongReasons: It sends data to all ports

questions.text: Which ACID property ensures that a transaction is either completed fully or not at all?
questions.explanation: Atomicity means all or nothing.
steps: Spot what the question tests: ACID properties.
Option A (Consistency) is out: Keeps the database valid.
Option C (Isolation) is out: Separates concurrent transactions.
Option D (Durability) is out: Keeps committed data permanent.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing consistency.
So the answer is option B: Atomicity.

questions.text: Which SQL join returns all rows from the left table and the matching rows from the right table, with NULLs where there is no match?
questions.explanation: A left outer join preserves unmatched rows from the left table.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Types of joins.
Option A (INNER JOIN) is out: Returns only matching rows.
Option C (RIGHT OUTER JOIN) is out: Keeps all rows of the right table.
Option D (CROSS JOIN) is out: Returns every combination of rows.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing INNER JOIN.
So the answer is option B: LEFT OUTER JOIN.
wrongReasons: Keeps all rows of the right table

questions.text: In an entity-relationship diagram, a diamond shape represents:
questions.explanation: Diamonds depict relationships between entities.
steps: Spot what the question tests: ER symbols.
Option B (An entity) is out: Shown by a rectangle.
Option C (An attribute) is out: Shown by an oval.
Option D (A key) is out: Shown by an underline.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing entity.
So the answer is option A: A relationship.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: The fourth condition is 'no pre-emption'; deadlock needs the absence of pre-emption, not pre-emption itself.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Conditions for deadlock.
Options B, C and D are out: A necessary condition.
Common slip to avoid: Missing the word 'no'.
So the answer is option A: Pre-emption.

questions.text: Compared with a process, a thread of the same process:
options: has its own separate address space
cannot run in parallel on multiple cores
shares the code and data of the process and is lighter to create
questions.explanation: Threads share the address space of their process.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Process vs thread.
Option A (has its own separate address space) is out: This is a process.
Option B (cannot run in parallel on multiple cores) is out: Threads can run in parallel.
Option C (is always slower to switch) is out: Thread switching is usually faster.
Common slip to avoid: Believing threads have separate address spaces.
So the answer is option D: shares the code and data of the process and is lighter to create.
questions.trap: Believing threads have separate address spaces.

questions.text: Which CPU scheduling algorithm can cause starvation of long processes if shorter processes keep arriving?
questions.explanation: SJF always prefers the shortest job, so long jobs may wait indefinitely.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Scheduling and starvation.
Option A (Round Robin) is out: Gives every process a time slice.
Option B (First Come First Served) is out: Serves in arrival order.
Option D (Multilevel feedback with ageing) is out: Ageing prevents starvation.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing FCFS.
So the answer is option C: Shortest Job First.
wrongReasons: Gives every process a time slice
